From: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Brady <t.brady@fintechco.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@fintechco.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Post-call: FintechCo integration & observability follow-up

Hi Tom / Alicia — thanks, and happy to take the tech lead on the call. Answers below + a short integration primer to help your infra and telemetry teams review in advance.

1) Auth patterns (server-to-server recommendations)
- Short answer: start with API keys for the POC, move to short-lived tokens or mTLS for production Dedicated/Private deployments.
  - API keys: supported in hosted flows. Use per-service (backend) keys scoped to routes; rotate regularly. We recommend keeping keys in your secrets manager and reading them at process start.
  - Short-lived tokens: Redwood supports OAuth2 client_credentials and token exchange for higher security; tokens are time-limited and reduce blast radius. We can help with sample code.
  - mTLS / private deployment: for VPC/Private deployments we support mutual TLS between your service and Redwood gateway — good for strict network controls.

2) SDK setup & routing
- SDK bootstrap (node):
  const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/inference');
  const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RDW_API_KEY, region: 'us-west-2' });
  
- Routing: the SDK accepts a routing hint object (preferred_model, fallback_model, preferred_region). Example: { routing: { preferred_model: 'redwood-chat-medium', fallback_model: 'redwood-chat-small', region: 'us-west-2' } }
- We also expose an explicit header 'X-RI-Region' you can set to force a region at request time. Fallbacks are automatic if capacity is constrained, and we instrument any fallback in the response headers.

3) Structured output / tool calling
- We support function/tool calling via JSON schema. You can define each tool signature and Redwood will return well-formed JSON when it chooses to call a tool. Example use cases: structured transaction extraction, sanboxing a re-ranking API, or returning an action payload for your investigator UI. We return both the generated JSON and a "tool_call" envelope in the response so you can log it separately.

4) Embeddings & rerankers
- Suggested flow for reranking:
  - Generate embeddings with model 'redwood-embed-large' (1024 dims)
  - Index in your vector DB (we see good tradeoffs with Faiss/HNSW for this workload)
  - At query time: do approximate KNN (k=50) then rerank top 10 using a cheap cross-encoder on Redwood (or use lightweight scoring in your service).
  - We can provide a small benchmark dataset and suggested thresholds for precision/recall.

5) Observability hooks (core ask) — recommended, supported fields and headers
- Trace ID headers: we support both standard and Redwood headers. Recommended to accept both so you can correlate across vendors:
  - traceparent (W3C Trace Context) — recommended if you run OpenTelemetry
  - X-RI-Trace-Id — Redwood-assigned 128-bit trace id returned with every response if not provided by caller
- Response latency breakdown headers (useful for dashboards / SLOs):
  - X-RI-Latency-Total: total server-side processing time (ms)
  - X-RI-Latency-Kernel: model kernel execution time (ms)
  - X-RI-Latency-Queue: time spent queued/waiting for GPU (ms)
  - X-RI-Latency-Network: egress time to underlying model shards (ms)
- Logging fields (we recommend including these in your request logs): request_id, user_id (app-level id), trace_id (from X-RI-Trace-Id / traceparent), model_name, model_version, token_count, latency_ms, backend_latency_ms, kv_cache_hits, rerank_candidate_count
- Example: when making a request include an 'x-request-id' you generate; we will echo it back along with X-RI-Trace-Id and the latency headers so your logs can do a join across services.
- Dashboards: we expose per-route metrics and traces in the Redwood Console and provide a Grafana dashboard you can pull into your observability stack. Example panels: 95th latency by route, fallback rate, cache hit %, and embedding index latency.

6) Attachments / docs
- SOC2 snapshot attached for security intake. I also attached a rough architecture diagram; we'll produce a cleaned-up version post-call.

I'll include a short checklist on the tech call: SDK quickstart, auth example, routing + fallback demo, embeddings/DB + rerank sketch, and wiring traces into Grafana. Proposed times still work for me Wednesday 10:30 PT.

Cheers,

Ethan Park
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
